titleEn: The Big Boy Holds the Bottle!

pages.text: "Mom, look at me! Look!" Pipo bounced in the shed. But Mom only held and patted a newborn lamb on the hay. "Shh, the lamb is sleeping." His smile drooped.
"I do not like the lamb! Mom only likes the lamb!" Pipo stamped. The bottle and hay bed were all the lamb's. "Hug me too..." He hid in the hay in a shed corner.
Inside the hay, it was dark and scratchy. Outside, the lamb bleated and Mom cooed. Only Pipo was alone. "...Maybe nobody can see me." He buried wet eyes against his knees.
Grandpa Sheep parted the hay with his stick. "Pipo, now you are the big boy. There is a job that needs big-boy hands." He held Pipo's hand tightly.
Grandpa led him beside Mom. The lamb cried baa, baa. "Why is it crying?" Pipo looked quietly. "Oh, because the bottle is over there?" It lay on hay farther away.
Pipo fetched the bottle and held it to the lamb's mouth with both hands. Suck, suck! It stopped crying and drank. Mom smiled. "The big boy holds the bottle! Pipo does it best."
"Mom! I made the lamb stop crying!" His shoulders rose and heart bounced. Crouching with hands at his chest, he said, "The big boy holds the bottle! I am best at this!"
Playing the big boy was fun. Pipo took both hands from his face—peekaboo! The lamb jumped. Now it followed only him.
Now Pipo knew big-boy jobs. "One, the big boy holds the bottle! Two, look when the lamb says baa! Three, sing a lullaby!" At his song, it gently closed its eyes.

Mom sat the lamb on one knee and Pipo on the other and hugged them. "Our Pipo is such a lovely big boy! A little one brings jobs for the big one." "The big boy holds the bottle!" Pipo stroked the lamb's head.
